source_citation: Cortez, P., & Morais, A. (2007). A Data Mining Approach to Predict Forest Fires using Meteorological Data. In New Trends in Artificial Intelligence, Proc. EPIA 2007, pp. 512–523. UCI repository: https://doi.org/10.24432/C5D88D. Montesinho park, Portugal.

inverse_for_reporting.raw_mean_lognormal_formula: exp(mu_z + sigma_z^2/2) - 1 under literal Normal on z
inverse_for_reporting.interval_caution: Intervals symmetric on log1p scale back-transform to asymmetric bounds on raw ha; do not claim symmetric raw-scale predictive intervals.
inverse_for_reporting.zero_inflation_caution: 47.8% exact zeros mean both median and mean back-transforms are model-based approximations, not population estimands.

primary_metrics: empirical interval coverage on log1p scale

allowed: RMSE/MAE on raw ha after back-transform
optional_raw_point_metrics.requirement: Predeclare whether predictions use expm1(mu_z) (raw median) or exp(mu_z + sigma_z^2/2)-1 (lognormal-style raw mean) before comparing to observed area.

metric_protocol.raw_area_normal_ngboost: Computably defined but scientifically misspecified — 47.8% zeros and heavy tail; not recommended as primary protocol. NLL on raw ha is not the primary metric.

target_distribution_log1p.note: Transform reduces skew but zeros map to 0.0 on log1p scale.

spatial_temporal_structure.spatial_dependence_note: Montesinho park grid cells (X 1–9, Y 2–9) repeat across months/days; optional (X,Y) group holdout for robustness.

distribution_assessment.normal_ngboost_on_raw_area: Scientifically misspecified as primary protocol — 47.8% exact zeros and extreme right skew make Normal on raw ha a poor generative model; NLL is computable but not recommended for primary comparison. Primary probabilistic metrics belong on log1p(area).
distribution_assessment.log1p_target_defensible: Yes as donor-aligned stress-test protocol; Normal on log1p(z) is still approximate because zeros map to z=0 (zero inflation).
distribution_assessment.stress_test_value: High for exposing homoscedastic vs natural-gradient behavior under misspecification and zero inflation; not suitable as primary calibration evidence.

preprocessing_recommendation.categoricals: Encode month and day (one-hot or ordinal label encoding for tree models); document encoding in pilot manifest.
preprocessing_recommendation.numeric: Use FFMC–rain as numeric; no mandatory scaling for trees.
preprocessing_recommendation.target: Primary pilot target: log1p(area). Primary NLL and coverage on log1p scale. Optional raw RMSE/MAE only after predeclaring expm1(mu_z) vs exp(mu_z+sigma_z^2/2)-1 back-transform.
preprocessing_recommendation.duplicates: Four exact duplicate rows observed — lead decision to drop or retain with disclosure before freeze.

primary_row_level_paper_aligned.approach: Row-level 90/10 holdouts, np.random.seed(1), fewer repetitions (e.g. 5–20) given n=517; identical splits across natural/ordinary/homoscedastic on log1p target.
primary_row_level_paper_aligned.leakage_risk: Moderate — same (X,Y) cell may appear in train and test across different dates.

optional_spatial_robustness.status: Optional subject-disjoint-style spatial holdout; not frozen.

prior_application_search.finding: NGBoost appears in other wildfire/remote-sensing work, but no documented NGBoost application on this UCI Montesinho table in bounded 2026-08-23 search; no official repo loader.
prior_application_search.limitation: Wildfire+NGBoost literature is large; dataset-specific claim only.

ethics_environmental.framing: Environmental wildfire burned-area regression; Montesinho Natural Park historical incidents; no personal identifiers.
ethics_environmental.requirements: Attribute Cortez/Morais and UCI; frame as stress test not operational fire prediction.

unresolved_concerns: Normal on raw ha is misspecified for primary use; log1p protocol must be frozen explicitly.
Back-transform mean vs median semantics and zero inflation must be disclosed in any raw-scale point metric.
Four duplicate rows and spatial repetition require pilot disclosure.
